summary_paragraph: A woman with Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence was admitted to the surgery service for one week of severe diffuse abdominal cramping with distension, loose stools, and one episode of clear emesis after recent gastrostomy tube change for leakage. She was evaluated with labs (including normal WBC and lactate) and abdominal imaging; abdominal radiographs were nonobstructive and CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast showed no obstruction, unchanged gastrostomy tube position in the gastric remnant, and no CT evidence of internal hernia. She was managed with observation, initial NPO status with IV hydration and antiemetics, then gradual re-trial of water and tube feeds with good tolerance, and transition to oral pain control. She remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable without signs of infection or bleeding and was discharged home ambulatory, tolerating Stage III diet and tube feeds, with instructions to avoid NSAIDs, crush pills, and follow up with her surgical team.
